mentions.name: Easel
mentions.description: Easel is a game programming language that makes games multiplayer automatically. Every program written in Easel is guaranteed deterministic and snapshottable, which the language uses to perform rollback netcode automatically. The rollback is incremental, storing deltas of only what has changed via a copy-on-write mechanism, making it efficient for games where players move through large worlds that are mostly dormant except near players. Current work focuses on making the multiplayer even more efficient so beginner coders can build large multiplayer games without worrying about it.
mentions.problem: Making multiplayer games is difficult for beginners, and raw coding needs to be fun and engaging for teenagers in the age of AI; automatic multiplayer lets learners build games with friends and family.
mentions.audience: Teenagers who love to play multiplayer games and beginner coders looking for a fun way to learn to code.
mentions.source_excerpt: For 4+ years I've been working on a game programming language which makes your game multiplayer automatically! Every program written in Easel is guaranteed deterministic and snapshottable, which it uses to automatically perform rollback netcode.

Developers can write code as if all players are in one shared world, like a singleplayer game, and Easel handles multiplayer state synchronization completely automatically. It is intended as a fun way for beginners to learn to code, like a combination of Scratch and Roblox.

mentions.name: Easel
mentions.description: A 2D game programming language designed to match how humans, not computers, think about game logic. Game-oriented features are first-class language constructs, such as behaviours where writing `on Pointer { ... }` creates a concurrently-executing coroutine with managed lifetime, giving the imperative language a declarative feel. Multiplayer is built into the language itself: anything written in Easel is automatically multiplayer, so creators can write code as if all players share one world, like a singleplayer game, while the engine handles multiplayer underneath. In development for 3 years.
mentions.problem: Multiplayer games normally require writing everything in a multiplayer-safe way — deterministic code that only modifies what your side has authority over; Easel removes that burden by putting multiplayer underneath all your lines of code in the language itself.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm making Easel, a 2D game programming language designed to match how humans, not computers, think about game logic. It also has automatic multiplayer. I've been working on it for 3 years!

evidence.value: I'm making Easel, a 2D game programming language designed to match how humans, not computers, think about game logic. It also has automatic multiplayer. I've been working on it for 3 years!
